external_entities.name: other teams' backend
external_entities.description: A backend operated by another product team that calls the inference gateway.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway
external_entities.notes: Two of the calling services are in a different cloud.

external_entities.name: ML engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who publishes new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
external_entities.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
external_entities.notes: The source is uncertain what governs who can push and says, 'I think it is a shared group account.'

processes.name: inference gateway
processes.description: A FastAPI service that receives inference requests, forwards them to the model server, and writes requests and responses to the inference log.
processes.source_excerpt: our inference gateway, a FastAPI service on GKE
processes.notes: It is exposed on the internet. Callers use API keys issued per calling team; the keys have never been expired.

processes.name: model server
processes.description: The server that runs the actual model on GPU nodes, loads model artifacts, and reads customer features.
processes.source_excerpt: the model server, which runs the actual model on GPU nodes in our model network
processes.notes: There is no authentication between the gateway and the model server. It uses its own service account to load model artifacts.

data_stores.name: model registry bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket holding model artifacts that the model server loads at startup.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.
data_stores.notes: The source says, 'I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket.'

data_stores.name: Redis feature store
data_stores.description: A Redis store containing customer features such as account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Redis feature store on the same network. ... The features include account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.notes: Redis has no password and is only reachable inside the model network.

data_stores.name: inference log
data_stores.description: A BigQuery log containing every request and response for debugging, including raw prompts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging.
data_stores.notes: Raw prompts sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

data_flows.name: call gateway
data_flows.description: The calling backend sends an inference request to the gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway
data_flows.notes: Callers pass an API key in a header. Keys are issued per calling team and have never been expired.

data_flows.name: forward request
data_flows.description: The gateway forwards an inference request to the model server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway forwards the request to the model server
data_flows.notes: There is no auth between the gateway and the model server.

data_flows.name: load artifacts
data_flows.description: The model server loads model artifacts from the registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.notes: The model server uses its own service account. The source says, 'I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket.'

data_flows.name: read features
data_flows.description: The model server reads customer features from Redis.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the model server reads from a Redis feature store on the same network
data_flows.notes: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.
data_flows.data_description: customer features including account age and spend bands per customer

data_flows.name: write logs
data_flows.description: The gateway writes every request and response to the inference log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery
data_flows.notes: The log is used for debugging. Raw prompts sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.
data_flows.data_description: every request and response, including raw prompts

data_flows.name: publish artifacts
data_flows.description: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source is unsure what governs who can push and says, 'I think it is a shared group account.'

trust_boundaries.name: GKE
trust_boundaries.description: The GKE environment where the inference gateway runs.

trust_boundaries.name: model network
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the GPU nodes running the model server and the Redis feature store.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: GPU nodes in our model network
trust_boundaries.notes: The model network is meant to be reachable only from the gateway.

assumptions.assumption: The inference gateway presents a web interface because it is described as a FastAPI service.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the component as a FastAPI service, which presents an HTTP application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The customer features in the Redis feature store are confidential because they are account age and spend bands associated with customers.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the features include 'account age and spend bands per customer'.

assumptions.assumption: The model server holds confidential customer-related data because it reads customer features.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the model server reads customer features including account age and spend bands per customer.
